title: Buying Pakistani Clothes From Abroad: A Guide
meta_description: Ordering Pakistani suits from the UK, US or Gulf — how to get sizing right, what to ask before paying, shipping and customs, and how returns really work.
keywords: buy Pakistani clothes online abroad, Pakistani suits UK US delivery, international shipping Pakistani clothes, ordering suits from Pakistan, customs duty clothes
excerpt: Ordering from Pakistan while living abroad works well when you ask the right four questions first. Most disappointments come from the same avoidable places.
imagePrompt: A neatly packed parcel of folded clothing in tissue paper on a pale wooden table, alongside a measuring tape, a printed measurement chart, a passport and a phone showing a blank screen. Soft even daylight from a window, shallow depth of field, calm organised editorial still life in warm neutrals, no faces, no text.

content.content:
Buying Pakistani clothing from London, Dubai, Toronto or Houston is now straightforward — most brands ship internationally, and the price difference against a diaspora boutique is substantial.

It is also where the largest share of disappointments happen, and they cluster around the same handful of causes: sizing that does not match any chart, fabric that is not what the listing said, delivery timed to miss the occasion, and a returns process that turns out to be impractical across a border.

None of these is unavoidable. Each of them comes down to a question asked before paying rather than after.

This is what to check, in the order that matters.

content.heading: Sizing: Do Not Trust the Chart
content.content:
Pakistani sizing is genuinely inconsistent between brands, and a size chart is a claim rather than a measurement.

**Measure a garment you already own and like**, laid flat: chest, waist, hip, shoulder seam to seam, sleeve length, total shirt length, trouser length and rise. Eight numbers, and they solve most of the problem.

**Ask the seller for the flat measurements of the actual item.** Not the size chart — the garment. Any seller with the stock in hand can tell you, and the ones who cannot are worth being cautious about.

**Compare against your own numbers**, not against a size label.

**Pay closest attention to the shoulder.** It is the measurement that cannot be altered cheaply, and the one that decides whether a garment looks right. Our post on [the five alterations that matter](/journal/five-alterations-make-any-suit-fit) covers what a tailor can and cannot fix.

**Order to fit the largest measurement.** Taking in is easy anywhere in the world; letting out is limited by the seam allowance.

Our [size guide](/content/size-guide) shows how ours are measured, and the guide to [picking a size in ready-to-wear](/journal/how-to-pick-size-pakistani-ready-to-wear) covers judging fit at a distance.

content.heading: Four Questions Before You Pay
content.content:
**One: what is the fabric, as a composition?** Not "silk-finish" or "premium quality" — a percentage. Most disappointment with online orders is a polyester arriving where silk was expected. Our guide on [telling real silk from fake](/journal/how-to-tell-real-silk-from-fake-pakistan) covers what the terms mean.

**Two: can you send a daylight video?** A short clip of the fabric moving in natural light shows colour, drape and sheen in a way a studio photograph does not. Most sellers will do this and it takes them a minute.

**Three: is it in stock now?** Made-to-order and pre-order are common and not always disclosed. This is the single biggest cause of missed deadlines.

**Four: what is the total landed cost?** Item, shipping, and any duty or tax at your end. A price that looks excellent can change substantially once customs is added.

A seller who answers all four clearly is a seller worth buying from. Vague answers to specific questions are information in themselves.

content.heading: Timing, Which Is Where Most Orders Fail
content.content:
International shipping from Pakistan is reliable but not fast, and it is seasonal.

**Allow four to six weeks** for a piece you need for a specific date, not two.

**Add two weeks around Eid and wedding season.** Volumes rise sharply, couriers slow, and everything takes longer. The weeks before both Eids are the worst.

**Add time for alterations at your end.** Ready-to-wear almost always needs some tailoring, and a tailor in London or Toronto needs a week or more in busy season.

**Ramadan slows everything**, including production and dispatch.

**Customs can add unpredictable days**, and there is no way to speed it up once it is in the system.

The practical version: **if the occasion is in six weeks, order now.** If it is in two weeks, buy locally. Our [shipping page](/help/shipping) has current timings, and the underlying advice — do not leave it to Chand Raat — applies doubly across a border.

content.heading: Customs, Duty and Paperwork
content.content:
Rules differ by country and change, so treat this as what to check rather than as fixed fact.

**Most countries have a value threshold** below which clothing arrives without duty. Above it, expect duty plus a handling fee from the courier.

**The handling fee is often the bigger surprise.** Couriers charge a fixed administrative fee for clearing a parcel, and on a small order it can exceed the duty itself.

**Ask how the parcel will be declared.** It should be declared accurately. Under-declaring is the seller's risk and yours, and a seized parcel is worse than a duty charge.

**Keep the invoice.** You will need it if the parcel is queried, and for any return.

**Check whether your country charges tax on the shipping cost too** — several do, which changes the calculation on a heavy parcel.

**Consolidate orders.** Several items in one parcel usually costs less in total than several parcels, both in shipping and in handling fees.

Our [payments page](/help/payments) covers the options available for international orders.

content.heading: Returns Across a Border
content.content:
This is the part to understand before ordering rather than after, because international returns are genuinely harder than domestic ones.

**Read the policy properly.** Time window, who pays return shipping, and whether stitched or altered items are eligible at all.

**Return shipping from abroad is expensive** and frequently exceeds the value of a single item.

**Customs on the way back** is its own process, and a returned parcel can attract charges in the other direction if it is not marked correctly.

**Exchange is often more practical than return.** Many sellers will exchange for a different size where they will not refund, and the shipping economics are better.

**Photograph the parcel on arrival**, before opening it fully. It is the only evidence you will have if something is wrong or missing.

**Do not alter anything until you are sure.** An altered garment is not returnable anywhere.

The practical conclusion: **the returns process is the reason to get sizing right up front.** Our [returns page](/help/returns) sets out where you stand with us, and it is worth reading the equivalent page before ordering anywhere.

content.heading: Stitched or Unstitched From Abroad
content.content:
The calculation is different when you live outside Pakistan, and it usually favours stitched.

**Unstitched is cheaper and lighter to ship**, and it gives a fit made to your measurements. But it needs a tailor who knows Pakistani cuts, and outside Pakistan those are harder to find and considerably more expensive — often enough to erase the saving entirely.

**It also shrinks.** Lawn and cotton shrink three to five percent in the first wash, so the fabric must be washed before stitching. Our [lawn buying guide](/journal/how-to-buy-lawn-well-pakistan-guide) covers this.

**Stitched removes all of that.** It arrives wearable, and any adjustment needed is a simple alteration rather than a full make-up — something any local tailor can handle.

**The middle path:** buy stitched, and budget for one small alteration at your end. This is what most people abroad settle on after doing it both ways.

Our post on [unstitched versus ready-to-wear](/journal/unstitched-vs-ready-to-wear-suits-pakistan) covers the wider trade-off, and the [stitched suits](/ladies/stitched-suits) section is where to look if you have decided.

content.heading: Ordering for Family in Pakistan
content.content:
The reverse case, and a common one: you are abroad and sending something home.

**Get their measurements properly**, not their size. A phone call and a tape measure takes five minutes and removes the entire problem.

**Confirm the delivery address and a working phone number.** Couriers in Pakistan call before delivering, and an unreachable number is the most common cause of a failed delivery.

**Order well ahead of Eid.** Domestic delivery slows just as international does.

**Consider who will be home.** Cash on delivery is common domestically and awkward if you are paying from abroad — check whether the seller takes an international card for a domestic delivery. Our [payments page](/help/payments) covers what we accept.

**Ask about gift packaging** if it is going directly to someone.

**Send a photograph of what you ordered** so they know what to expect and can flag immediately if something is wrong, while the return window is still open.

And if you are choosing for someone else, the [Virtual Try Room](/virtual-try-room) is a reasonable way to judge how a colour will look before committing. The full range is in the [ladies collection](/ladies), with [kids](/kids) and [baby](/baby) alongside.

questions.question: How do I get the size right ordering Pakistani clothes from abroad?
questions.answer: Measure a garment you already own and like, laid flat — chest, waist, hip, shoulder seam to seam, sleeve, shirt length, trouser length and rise. Then ask the seller for the flat measurements of the actual item rather than their size chart, and compare against your numbers.

questions.question: How long does shipping from Pakistan take?
questions.answer: Allow four to six weeks for a specific date, and add two weeks around Eid and wedding season when volumes rise and couriers slow. Add time for alterations at your end too. If the occasion is in two weeks, buy locally rather than ordering.

questions.question: Will I pay customs duty on clothes from Pakistan?
questions.answer: It depends on your country's value threshold. Above it, expect duty plus a courier handling fee — and the handling fee is often the bigger surprise, since it is fixed regardless of order size. Consolidating several items into one parcel usually costs less in total.

questions.question: Should I buy stitched or unstitched if I live abroad?
questions.answer: Usually stitched. Unstitched is cheaper to ship but needs a tailor familiar with Pakistani cuts, who is harder to find and much more expensive outside Pakistan — often enough to erase the saving. It also shrinks and must be washed before stitching.

questions.question: Can I return an item internationally?
questions.answer: Check the policy before ordering, because return shipping from abroad frequently exceeds the value of a single item and the parcel faces customs in the other direction too. Exchange is often more practical than refund. Never alter anything until you are certain you are keeping it.
